ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is trapezoid QRST, the upper base TS and the lower base QR are both drawn as horizontal lines and are parallel to each other; T is at the upper left, S is at the upper right, Q is at the lower left, and R is at the lower right. The left leg is TQ, and the right leg is SR. A and B are respectively on the two legs, and AB is a horizontal midline. In the figure, the interior angle at vertex T is marked as 120°. Reasoning: Because TS ∥ QR, the left leg TQ is a transversal, so the same-side interior angles ∠T and ∠Q are supplementary. Given ∠T = 120°, therefore m∠Q = 180° - 120° = 60°.

raw_record.question_text: For trapezoid $Q R S T$, $A$ and $B$ are midpoints of the legs. Find $m\angle Q$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as trapezoid QRST with horizontal parallel bases TS and QR. The image shows the interior angle at T labeled 120°. Since TS ∥ QR in a trapezoid, the left leg TQ is a transversal, so consecutive interior angles ∠T and ∠Q are supplementary. Compute m∠Q = 180° - 120° = 60°.
